claims.claim: Liaison Strategies poll of 1,000 Toronto residents Oct. 8-9, 2026 puts Chow at 51 per cent and Bradford at 46 per cent among decided and leaning voters, with 3 per cent backing another candidate
The Liaison margin of error for the total sample is plus or minus 3.1 percentage points, 19 times out of 20
Chow's lead narrowed from eight points in Liaison's Oct. 6 poll to five points, after Chris Alexander left the race
Nanos poll for CP24 and CTV News Toronto, 757 Toronto residents Oct. 8-10, puts Chow at 51 and Bradford at 47 among decided voters, a 3.5-point gap, with 17 per cent undecided
claims.attributed_to: Nanos Research for CP24/CTV News Toronto

claims.claim: Liaison finds Chow leading renters 57-40 and Bradford leading homeowners 50-45
Chow's approval stands at 52 per cent, disapproval 43 per cent, unsure 5 per cent
Bradford's favourability is 37 per cent favourable and 40 per cent unfavourable among all respondents
More than 222,000 eligible voters cast advance ballots before advance voting closed Oct. 11, the city's biggest advance turnout in over a decade
claims.attributed_to: City of Toronto, via NOW Toronto and CBC News

claims.claim: Election day is Monday, Oct. 26, 10 a.m. to 8 p.m., with 361 candidates certified by the Toronto City Clerk on Aug. 24
Chow and Bradford are certified mayoral candidates, nominated May 25 and May 1 respectively
claims.attributed_to: Wikipedia, citing City of Toronto certified candidate list

claims.claim: The Oct. 15 debate hosted by the Rotman School of Management and TVO, moderated by Steve Paikin, is the campaign's final scheduled debate
Both candidates campaigned in Scarborough this week, Chow on transit and the Scarborough East LRT, Bradford on homeownership costs and city spending
Polls disagree on Scarborough and North York, so no single regional read holds
The City of Toronto says 222,550 eligible voters cast ballots during six days of advance voting, Oct. 6-11, a record
Advance turnout was up nearly 92 per cent from the 115,911 advance votes in 2022
Sunday, Oct. 11 was the single busiest advance day at 53,363, the highest one-day advance total since amalgamation
Chow said people told her they voted for her, giving her confidence; Bradford said the turnout shows change is coming
Advance voting numbers do not indicate which candidates voters selected
Chow leads Bradford 51 to 46 among decided and leaning voters, Liaison Strategies poll of 1,000 residents Oct. 8-9, margin of error plus or minus 3.1 points
Nanos poll for CP24 and CTV News Toronto had Chow 51 to Bradford 47 among decided voters
claims.attributed_to: Nanos Research for CP24/CTV News Toronto

claims.claim: CP24 reported the advance total as 225,550, which does not match the city's 222,550 figure carried by other outlets
Election day is Monday, Oct. 26, polls open 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.
No revised advance turnout figure has been issued; the City of Toronto's released total remains 222,550 over six days of advance voting, Oct. 6-11
CityNews, Global News and the Toronto Sun all carry the city's 222,550 figure
The city's news release list shows no advance-turnout release dated after Oct. 13
CP24 gives the advance total as 225,550, which does not match the city's 222,550 carried by other outlets
CBC reports advance turnout as nearly 72 per cent above the 2023 byelection's 129,745 advance votes
The nearly 92 per cent comparison is measured against the 115,911 advance votes in 2022

Liaison analysis: Downtown held 40 per cent of the advance vote while holding a bit over a third of voters; North York's share rose 24.9 to 27.8 per cent and Scarborough's fell 21.2 to 19.1 per cent; Etobicoke unchanged
Eglinton-Lawrence led wards in early turnout at about 15,000 ballots, 16.7 per cent of its electorate; citywide advance participation was 10.4 per cent
No city statement correcting, withdrawing or restating the 222,550 figure was found
